title: Plugin cards and side panels
intro: Some installed plugins add a dashboard card or a side panel. Use a side panel to keep the plugin visible while moving between app pages.
You see a plugin card and panel only when you may see that plugin. A plugin restricted to certain roles keeps those same restrictions here.
Administrators with marketplace management access can switch a card or panel off for everyone in the lab. The plugin page and other work remain enabled.

Use a plugin your organisation already installed. The pictures use the optional Reference Plugin on a test installation. Light theme keeps this sample plugin readable. No clinical sample data is needed.

tasks.title: Read a plugin dashboard card
intro: A plugin must declare a dashboard card before one can appear. Its content comes from that plugin.
steps: Read the plugin card beneath the dashboard widgets. Cards appear on dashboards outside the normal widget editor. You cannot move or resize them there.
tasks.result: The reference example reports Drawn in: widget. Your plugin shows its own content.

tasks.title: Open a panel while you work
intro: A panel is available only when an enabled plugin declares one and you may access that plugin.
steps: Select the Side panels button beside the notification bell. It appears only when a panel is available.
Select its title. The example is Reference panel.
The panel opens on the right. The main page remains available beside it on desktop.
Choose another page in the main menu. The panel stays open with its current content. The example moves to Forms.
Select Close at the panel top right.
tasks.result: Closing returns the space to the main page. Signing out or disabling the plugin or its panel also closes it.

tasks.title: Switch a card or panel off
intro: These switches apply to the whole lab. Each switch saves immediately. There is no separate Save action.
steps: Choose the installed plugin that supplies the card or panel.
Select Places. This action appears only when the plugin declares a dashboard card or side panel.
Turn Dashboard card off to hide that card. Turn it on to restore it.

tasks.title: Control the side panel separately
intro: Continue in Places. Each placement switch controls that one location; it does not disable the whole plugin.
steps: An off switch means the dashboard card is hidden. A failed save reports an error and keeps the previous state.
Turn Side panel off to hide that panel. It has a separate switch.
Close Places and return to Dashboard. The example has hidden both places, while Reference Plugin remains in the main menu.
tasks.result: The plugin page and its other work remain enabled. Each change appears in Audit as plugin.sites.update.

tasks.title: Use a side panel on a phone
intro: At phone width, the panel covers the main page beneath the app header.
steps: Open the header Side panels button and choose the panel.
Use the panel content. The underlying page is covered.
Select Close at the panel top right.
tasks.result: The screenshots verify the 375px layout. A real phone must confirm access around retractable browser chrome.

end.title: Read or change places from the CLI
paragraphs: Follow Start here for CLI setup. From openldr_ce, use the plugin id. A place is called widget for Dashboard card and panel for Side panel.
html:
pnpm openldr market sites <plugin-id>
pnpm openldr market sites <plugin-id> widget off
pnpm openldr market sites <plugin-id> widget on
pnpm openldr market sites <plugin-id> panel off
pnpm openldr market sites <plugin-id> panel on

end.title: Optional practice with Reference Plugin
paragraphs: Use your own installed plugin for normal work. In a disposable source installation, the reference plugin demonstrates a card, panel and separate plugin page. Build tools need Rust and its wasm32-wasip1 target.

From openldr_ce, run pnpm build:ui-reference, then pnpm openldr plugin install reference-plugins/ui-reference/plugin.wasm. Reload Studio. Dashboard shows Reference card and Side panels offers Reference panel. The reference plugin declares no publisher signature, so use it only in a test installation.
The picture reads Drawn in: widget or Drawn in: panel according to its location. Its test note is fictional. Remove it afterward with pnpm openldr plugin remove ui-reference.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: No Side panels button. Check that an enabled, permitted plugin declares a panel and its Side panel switch is on.
No Places action. That plugin may not declare a card or panel. Places does not add a new capability to a plugin.
The card is missing. Check Dashboard card in Places, the plugin enabled state and your role access.
The reference sample is hard to read. Use light theme. The sample has fixed dark text; this preview does not change plugin source.

end.title: Related guides
paragraphs: Marketplace covers installation and plugin state. Dashboards covers ordinary dashboard widgets.
